account:
Something unusually large is being arranged for this evening, but I do not yet know its real occasion. Innkeeper requested a precise six o'clock appointment in the town hall great hall, with secretary escorting me. I approved six to six-thirty. The recorded subject is civic hospitality and community gatherings, but the committee's names and detailed agenda have still not been supplied despite requests.

Refreshments appear substantial: secretary reported an original order of 120 loaves with payment unverified, and an additional 80 paid for by builder. I heard builder asking to carry the final 32 loaves from his paid order. Neighbour now tells me innkeeper said that he, freight, and builder ordered the refreshments. Neighbour also asked whether the gathering was open to everyone but received no answer she could make out. She does not know the occasion either.

Secretary has been checking the payment without authorizing treasury funds. No council correspondence was available for my one o'clock appointment. I asked innkeeper directly about tonight's proposals, but have not heard an intelligible answer. These omissions make the gathering feel secretive, though they do not prove wrongdoing. It may simply be a community celebration or hospitality event, possibly a surprise involving me; that is only speculation. I have no confirmed evidence of proposed bridge or port changes or misuse of town money.

I have just finished my scheduled tea at neighbour's dockside cottage. It is 16:02, and I should return for my 16:30 office appointment, obtain any secretary updates, and keep the six o'clock meeting.
